title: NEURAL COMPRESSION FOR IMPROVED BANDWIDTH AND POWER CONSUMPTION EFFICIENCY EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo improve compression performance identify statistical properties of data using ML, yielding improved data throughput and science utility.DescriptionNeural compression methods for astronomical data can enhance compression performance by exploiting mission-specific statistical properties. Unlike generic entropy coders, neural models incorporate advanced probability estimators that adapt to uniquedata distributions observed in cosmic measurements. These architectures often leverage autoencoder or diffusion frameworks, parameterizing the probability density of input samples with high fidelity. Consequently, the model can produce compact representationswhile ensuring bit-level accuracy is preserved. Reduced data volume translates to lower bandwidth consumption, mitigating bandwidth constraints and lessening reliance on highpower transmission components. Onboard, power requirements for data handlingdecrease, allowing systems to allocate energy resources more efficiently for other mission criticaloperations. Additionally, neural compression frameworks can be retrained or finetuned to reflect new observational conditions, maintaining optimal performance as mission parameters change. Overall, this approach can yield notable gains in data throughput, resource allocation, and scientific utility in scenarios where preserving exactmeasurements while minimizing data transmission is imperative.Tasks of the activity:Task 1: State-of-the-Art Analysis- Conduct a comprehensive analysis of classical (including CCSDS compressionstandards) and AI-based compression algorithms relevant to astronomical data. This includes consideringon-the-fly compression errors monitoring and fallback strategies to classical methods.Task 4: Implementation and Deployment- Implement and deploy the algorithms on a representative board.Task 5: Verification and Validation- Verify and validate the implementation, including assessment on the performance of AIbasedmethods compared to classical algorithms.

title: SYSTEM PHASE A STUDY - NGGM
description: In the frame of the Missions of Opportunity enabled by international cooperation, ESA and NASA have coordinated studies of gravity monitoring constellations optimised to observe mass changes and transport in the Earth system. In 2016 the report from the ESA-NASA Interagency Gravity Science Working Group defined the benefits of such a unique cooperative effort. The objective of the NGGM - NextGeneration Gravity Mission (also known as MAGIC - for Mass-change and Geosciences International Constellation ) is the long-term monitoring of the temporal variations of Earth's gravity field at high resolution in time (down to 3 days) and space (100 km). NGGM/MAGIC will observe Earth mass change and reinforce services by monitoring hydrology, cryosphere, oceanography, solid Earth and climatechange. This gravity mission evolution will provide continuity of science and services with respect to predecessor missions like GRACE, GOCE and GRACE Follow-On and will complement other ESA Earth Explorer programme and Copernicus missions. This activity corresponds with the Phase A system studies, whose main objective will be the determination of the programmatic, technical and technological feasibility of the mission within its boundary conditions.
